- **Immune-mediated destruction of red blood cells (autoimmune haemolytic anaemia)** — this causes pallor, jaundice, tiredness, lightheadedness, and characteristically **dark (not pale) stools** because excess bilirubin pigment is dumped into the bowel.
- **Immune-mediated hepatitis (liver inflammation)** — which also causes jaundice and fatigue.

These can occur together, and both are treatable but need prompt identification. I'll now run a targeted set of tests to separate them: a blood count, markers of red cell breakdown, liver tests, a Coombs test (which detects antibodies stuck onto your red cells), a look at your red cells under the microscope, and a urine test.

message.content:
That final result completes the picture. I now have everything I need.

**Summary of findings:**
| Finding | Result | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|
| Total bilirubin | 61 µmol/L, **72% unconjugated** | Indirect (haemolytic) jaundice — not bile duct obstruction |
| Reticulocytes | 261.7 ×10⁹/L (**23.7%**) | Marrow responding vigorously → haemolysis, not marrow failure |
| LDH | 1214 U/L | Massive red cell breakdown |
| Haptoglobin | <0.3 g/L | Consumed by free haemoglobin |
| Blood film | Spherocytes, reticulocytosis | Antibody-mediated extravascular haemolysis |
| DAT (Coombs) | **IgG 2+, C3d 5+**; IAT panreactive, no alloantibodies | Autoantibody against own red cells |
| Exam | Pale, deeply icteric, afebrile, no abdominal pain | Anaemia + jaundice without infection or biliary colic |

The **unconjugated** bilirubin rules out obstructive/pale-stool jaundice, and explains your **dark stools** — excess bilirubin pigment is converted to stercobilin in the gut. Your lethargy and lightheadedness come from the falling haemoglobin, and the jaundice from the pigment load.

The timing is decisive: symptoms began **14 days after your first pembrolizumab infusion**. Checkpoint inhibitors release the brakes on T-cells, which can then permit autoantibody production against red cell antigens — a recognised, though uncommon, immune-related adverse event.
